name: Byron Donalds
role: U.S. Representative for Florida's 19th district (2021-present); Florida state representative (2016-2020); Republican nominee for Governor of Florida in 2026
summary: A conservative Republican and Freedom Caucus member who backs lower taxes and spending cuts, gun rights, restricted immigration, school choice, domestic oil, gas and nuclear energy, and opposition to abortion and gender-identity law. He is skeptical of international bodies and foreign aid, though a strong supporter of Israel, and is allied with Donald Trump's agenda.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His House issue page calls the ACA a route to 'a single-payer socialist system' and rejects federally imposed healthcare; in 2025 Oversight remarks he again describes the ACA as designed to move the country to single payer.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In February 2021 he called the $15 federal minimum wage in the American Rescue Plan one of its 'radical and misguided' policies; he voted No on the ARP (2021-49).

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His healthcare page asks for 'the free market to prosper and work as intended'; he argued in committee that government-run grocery stores have less stock and worse food; his gubernatorial economy plank frames Florida as light on regulation. Stated for specific sectors, not as a general principle.

public-ownership.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Voted Yes on H.R. 1 (2025-145, 2025-190) extending and adding tax cuts, No on Build Back Better (2021-385) and the 2022 reconciliation bill (2022-420); cosponsored estate-tax repeal and the FairTax (income-tax repeal).

unions-good.rationale: Called the PRO Act a 'radical union boss wish list' and 'mega-donor' handout, voted No (2021-70), and cosponsored union free-choice bills in 2022, 2024 and 2025 and opposition to the PRO Act's repeal of right-to-work laws; voted No on the Faster Labor Contracts Act (2026-216).

regulate-corporations.rationale: Authored the Repeal CFPB Act to abolish the consumer finance regulator, called the SEC climate disclosure rule 'agency overreach into businesses', and voted No on the ESG Disclosure Simplification Act (2021-169).

limit-guns.rationale: His House page says 'Shall Not Be Infringed, means Shall Not Be Infringed'; he called H.R. 8 and H.R. 1446 infringements, and voted No on background-check, assault-weapon, red-flag and 'Protecting Our Kids' bills (2021-75, 2021-77, 2022-255, 2022-245, 2022-410).

empower-police-military.rationale: Cosponsored resolutions backing police, authored the D.C. CRIMES Act and voted for DoD and DHS appropriations (2024-331, 2024-333, 2025-212), but voted No on the FY2022 and FY2023 defense authorization bills (2021-293, 2022-350) and the final 2023 NDAA (2023-723).

decide-locally.rationale: Mixed: he argues abortion and election rules belong to the states and cosponsored abolishing the Education Department, but he authored D.C. legislation, backs nationwide Voter ID and national border measures.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted No on the Respect for Marriage Act both times (2022-373, 2022-513); no stated reasoning found.

abortion-legal.rationale: Calls himself 'an advocate for the pro-life movement', welcomed Dobbs, said he will vote NO on any effort to expand abortion access, and voted Yes on the Born-Alive Act (2023-29, 2025-27) and No on the Women's Health Protection Act (2021-295, 2022-360). Does not state what legal limits he wants.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Said history on race 'deserves the proper attention' but opposed critical race theory and equity training as dividing Americans; cosponsored bills ending DEI and disparate-impact claims.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said critical race theory and 'so-called equity training' threaten to degrade 'American values and culture'; stated in opposing CRT, not as a general doctrine of cultural preservation.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Said the WHO 'should have zero say over any policy related to our nation', and cosponsored bills barring funds for UN agencies and the WHO pandemic treaty.

free-trade.rationale: Said earlier trade deals put American companies and workers behind other countries and backs the tariff reset; he has not addressed free trade's long-run benefits as such.

nation-first.rationale: Said 'We take care of America at home, we can talk about the world, but America's got to be taken care of first', and closed his Maduro statement with 'put America First'.

open-borders.rationale: Said on the House floor that 'borders are essential to our sovereignty and security'; introduced border and visa-overstay bills; rejects amnesty.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Cosponsored measures against a carbon tax, climate disclosure rules, climate national emergencies and climate envoy funding, and a 2024 resolution condemning the UN climate agreement to move away from fossil fuels; criticized 'Green New Deal leftists'.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Introduced a multi-bill nuclear energy package and the Build Nuclear With Local Materials Act, and wrote an op-ed defending nuclear power and waste management.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Cosponsored repeal of the estate and generation-skipping taxes in 2024 (H.R. 7035) and 2025 (H.R. 1301) and reduction of estate and gift taxes in 2026 (H.R. 601). Cosponsorship only, so medium.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Said in August 2025 that the president 'has used tariff policy to reset the trade balance' so American companies and workers are no longer behind other nations, and that tariffs are a negotiating tool.

military-superiority.rationale: Described the Maduro operation as 'Peace Through Strength' and voted for the 2025 defense appropriations (2025-212); no direct statement on superiority over rivals.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said he voted for Florida's 2019 law defining antisemitism to include denying that Israel is the Jewish people's ancestral homeland; voted for 'Reaffirming the State of Israel's right to exist' (2023-677) and cosponsored a 2021 resolution on Israel's capital and self-determination.

school-vouchers.rationale: His House page backs school choice initiatives and his governor platform says 'Let education money follow the student so parents can choose the best school'; cosponsored a charter school tax credit (H.R. 2798, 2026).

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Called the $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan a bailout and 'fiscally irresponsible', said it would force future cuts, introduced the RESCUE Act in response, and voted No (2021-49, 2021-72).

force-without-un.rationale: Said the president has constitutional authority to strike Iran and that the War Powers Act does not obstruct him; welcomed the 2026 capture of Maduro; voted No on repeated Iran, Venezuela and Lebanon war powers resolutions (2025-345, 2026-48, 2026-114, 2026-282). UN approval is not discussed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Cosponsored H.R. 6854 (no federal public benefits for aliens) and H.R. 7817 (ACA subsidies only for citizens and lawfully present aliens); his governor platform would cut state benefits that encourage illegal immigration. Cosponsor-based, so medium.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: His House energy page commits to legislation encouraging American oil and gas and lifting burdensome regulations; he voted Yes on the Lower Energy Costs Act (2023-182) and attacked 'Green New Deal leftists' for curbing energy supply.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: His 2025 letter to Senate leadership asks for a legal immigration system that prioritizes 'merit, skills, and assimilation'. He does not say immigrants must give up their culture.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said constituents 'feel lied to and sold down the river by Washington politicians' and that he would not be 'hoodwinked by party insiders, the swamp, or the uniparty'; called the CFPB 'corrupt, unelected bureaucracy'.

separated-powers.rationale: Invokes checks and balances (on student loans and abortion) and cosponsored a nine-justice Supreme Court amendment, but urged ending the legislative filibuster and cosponsored impeaching a federal judge.

death-penalty.rationale: His campaign told the press he 'firmly supports the death penalty' for the state; reported secondhand from a campaign statement.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Voted Yes on the rescissions package that defunded USAID, calling its spending 'farcical' (2025-168); voted No on the Global Malnutrition Prevention Act (2022-137) and the Haiti development bill (2022-66); cosponsored bills barring US contributions to UN refugee and relief agencies.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Cosponsored H.R. 925 (end DEI programs) and H.R. 8445 (cut federal funds to schools considering race), and said equity training divides Americans. Cosponsorship plus statement.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Voted No on removing Confederate statues and the Taney bust from the Capitol (2021-196), but cosponsored replacing the Taney bust with one of Clarence Thomas (H.R. 4216), so the record points both ways.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Cosponsored H.R. 4448 (2026) to bar disparate-impact claims. Cosponsorship only.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Argued the WHO regulations must go through the Senate under the Constitution, cosponsored a bar on funds to implement the WHO pandemic treaty (2023) and ICC sanctions (2024).

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Opposed the Equality Act as 'politically manufacturing biological science'; cosponsored bills banning gender-affirming care for minors and housing prisoners by biological sex regardless of gender identity.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Voted No on the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act (2022-33) and the Speak Out Act (2022-480). Votes only.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Cosponsored resolutions in 2021 and 2023 condemning calls to defund, disband, dismantle or abolish police.

term-limits.rationale: Cosponsored congressional term-limit constitutional amendments in 2021, 2023 and 2025 (H.J.Res. 12, 11, 12). Cosponsorship only.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voted to disapprove D.C.'s noncitizen local voting law (2023-118) and for bills barring noncitizen voting in D.C. (2024-232, 2025-163); cosponsored H.R. 8218 requiring citizenship to vote in municipal elections. Votes and cosponsorship only.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Defended gun owners' right 'to defend their families' as a constitutional right in his H.R. 1446 statement, which presupposes lawful defensive force. Close inference from a stated view.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Said Washington should not 'politically manufacture biological science' and that 'political science will never replace actual science' in opposing gender provisions of H.R. 5.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Said a central bank digital currency would give bureaucrats 'absolute control over your money' and voted for the CBDC ban (2025-201). He did not address private payments' untraceability.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Voted Yes on the resolution that a carbon tax would harm the economy (2024-97) and cosponsored it and a 2021 version.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: His House page pledges to sponsor and pass a Balanced Budget Amendment requiring both chambers to pass a balanced budget annually; he voted Yes on the Limit, Save, Grow Act's spending caps (2023-199); his gubernatorial plank says Tallahassee must balance its books every year.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Called Biden's plan to cancel student loan debt 'unconstitutional' and welcomed the Supreme Court blocking it as a victory for those who paid off or never took loans.

public-service-media.rationale: Voted to defund NPR and PBS in the 2025 rescissions package, saying he objected to 'the egregious politicization of reporting at federally-funded news outlets'.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: His D.C. CRIMES Act removes judicial discretion to sentence youth offenders below the mandatory minimum. It is about minimums for a set of offenders, not specifically repeat offenders.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Said the PRO Act would overturn right-to-work laws 'forcing workers to fund labor unions they do not wish to join'; cosponsored free-choice-of-membership bills (H.R. 1275, 1200, 1232).

voter-id.rationale: Voted for the SAVE Act proof-of-citizenship bill (2025-102) and cosponsored it; praised the House's 2026 'nationwide Voter ID' bill as 'common-sense'; opposed H.R. 1 in 2021 partly because it would abolish voter identification laws.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Cosponsored H.R. 8282 (2024) to sanction the ICC for investigating US or allied protected persons. Cosponsorship only.

notes: Living person: no inference was used. Answers rest on House roll-call votes, cosponsorships in the Congressional Record Index, and his own press releases, hearing transcripts, op-eds and campaign platform. Where cosponsorship or a vote is the only basis the answer is medium. Updates: his early Ukraine votes were mixed (Yes on the 2022 lend-lease bill), then he opposed Ukraine funding from 2023 on; Ukraine is not scored because no statement matches exactly. He voted to object to the 2020 electoral votes of Arizona and Pennsylvania (2021-10, 2021-11) and against the January 6 commission (2021-154), but no statement was answered from this. Ran for the governor nomination and won the August 2026 primary (per Wikipedia).
